To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sovereign credit ratings for 18 countries are quantifiable in terms of a single variable proxying for debt management history.
the probability of default of a sovereign is a function of its past debt management history and of its current macroeconomic and political situation.

(i) the sovereign creditworthiness of a country is a function of its debt management history, the current macroeconomic and financial environment, and its future prospects, and (ii) a credit rating should be based on a proxy for debt managemen t histories and summaries of the most recent available information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most relevant explanatory variables, the most appropriate statistical methods of analysis, and the most effective ways of summarising and communicating the results of SRA.

the development of a more realistic and comprehensive SRA model that is capable of quantifying sovereign credit ratings in a manner that can be used to assist in the management of sovereign debt and the formulation of sovereign debt policy.
the development and application of a new statistical approach to SRA which can be used to quantify the degree of solvency of a state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art is not yet fully mature.
SRA should be more than the application of statistical models to historical data.
the most appropriate and reliable SRA is a combination of the best of both the statistical and the judgmental approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a more comprehensive approach is required for SRA.
the most important factors in sovereign risk analysis are the macroeconomic conditions of the country, the political stability, and the degree of institutional development of the country.
the use of a single explanatory variable is insufficient and that the choice of the appropriate functional form is crucial to the quality of the analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the most important explanatory variables are the country's debt management history, the country's economic and fiscal fundamentals, and the country's external debt service burden. (JEL C14, C22, E44, E62, G15, G18, G32, G38)
the use of a single variable as a proxy for debt history, and a single explanatory variable as a proxy of macroeconomic performance, is not sufficient.
the current practices in the field are not sufficiently robust. (JEL: C23, G15, O17)
